conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and diversifying holdings. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure and meet the combined limit.
Reduce SPY to 25% to cure the concentration flag and meet the single name mandate.
Buy MRVL at 4% of the book, leveraging a top-scoring scanner setup.
Increase QQQ to 20% to maintain broad index exposure and balance the portfolio.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a high-quality new name. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a blend of growth and stability.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration flag and meet the single name mandate.
Add to SOXL, targeting 6% of the book, and SPAL, targeting 6%, to increase leveraged exposure within limits.
Buy MRVL at 6% of the book, leveraging a top-scoring scanner setup.
Buy TECL at 5% of the book, adding another strong leveraged tech setup.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and high-scoring setups, increasing both upside potential and drawdown risk. Be aware of significant volatility, potential for rapid losses, and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book, to prioritize income and steady distributions.

income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth by rotating into income-focused ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, these are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
